resource.id: from the export: the resource is changed in place — only the keys present in the document; without "id" a new one is created. A document from elsewhere (another parish, a template): remove "id"
resource.key: a short name (letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 characters) for references within this document, e.g. "parent": "@house"
resource.area: the area of the resource: an id from the export or the exact name of an area you write in. A new resource without "area" goes to the area chosen at import; an existing one cannot be moved
resource.areaName: the name of the area — information only (export), the import ignores it
resource.name: name, 1–{max} characters (required for a new one), e.g. “Meetings with Fr. Peter”, “St Joseph's House”
resource.kind: kind: {list}; a new one without it — "other"
resource.mode: "offered" — the office offers slots and the person chooses one of them (meetings with the priest); "open" — the person asking chooses the time (a hall, a house). A new one without it — "offered"
resource.parent: inside another resource of the same area (a room in a house): "@key" from this document or "id"; null — separate. Whoever takes the whole also takes the parts, and the other way round
resource.calendar: only "offered": the calendar holding the slots — "id" or the exact name of a calendar in the resource's area. A new "offered" resource without it gets a new calendar named like the resource. Every meeting in this calendar is a slot to choose (cf. "bookableDefault")
resource.capacity: "offered": how many people per slot; "open": how many groups at a time (1–{max}); a new one without it — 1
resource.approval: "none" — whoever fits, has it; "office" — the office confirms each request separately. A new one without it — "none"
resource.perPerson: how many slots one person may hold at a time; 0 — no limit (0–1000)
resource.inviteHours: only "offered": for how many hours the first person to sign up is the host of the slot and picks the others themselves (by code or consent); 0 — no host (0–1440)
resource.minPersons: only "offered" with a host: from how many people a group keeps the slot for itself after the host time (1–1000; a new one without it — 2)
resource.byNight: only "open": true — time counted in nights (a house), false — in hours (a hall)
resource.checkIn: only "open" by night: arrival from "HH:MM" (a new one without it — "16:00")
resource.checkOut: only "open" by night: departure by "HH:MM" (a new one without it — "10:00")
resource.bufferBefore: only "open": minutes of preparation before each group (0–1440)
resource.bufferAfter: only "open": minutes of cleaning after each group (0–1440)
resource.leadDays: only "open": at least how many days before the start one can ask; 0 — as long as it is not in the past (0–3650)
resource.bookableDefault: only "offered": true — every meeting in the resource's calendar is a slot to choose; false — only those with "bookable": true
resource.reserveArea: who may book: an area id (its people and the areas under it); null — anyone who finds the slot
resource.slots: only "offered": slots to choose (below), at most {max} in the document
resource.claims: export only: the reservations the office sees (below) — the import does not change them

slot.id: from the export: the slot (the whole series) is changed in place — only the keys present in the document; without "id" a new one is created in the resource's calendar
slot.title: title, up to {max} characters; empty — “Slot” (the person choosing sees the resource name and the time)
slot.start: start "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" in local time; "YYYY-MM-DD" — all day. Required for a new one
slot.end: end: "HH:MM" on the same day or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM"; for all day the last day "YYYY-MM-DD". A new one without it lasts an hour (all day — one day); a changed "start" without "end" keeps the length
slot.every: every how many days / weeks / months / years (1–52); missing — 1
slot.weekdays: with "weekly": days of the week, e.g. ["wt", "cz"] — "pn", "wt", "śr", "cz", "pt", "so", "nd" (Mon … Sun); missing — the day of "start"
slot.until: last day of the series "YYYY-MM-DD"; a series without "until" and "count" lasts 10 years
slot.notes: a note for those who run the calendar, up to {max} characters
slot.link: a link to information ("https://…" or "#/…"), up to {max} characters
slot.linkLabel: the text on the link button, up to {max} characters
slot.capacity: own number of places of this slot (1–{max}); null — as the resource
slot.bookable: true — can be chosen, false — not (an ordinary meeting in the calendar); null — as the resource's "bookableDefault"
slot.reserveArea: only this group can take it: an area id; null — as the resource

claim.slot: "id" of the slot it concerns ("offered" mode); null — a time chosen by the person asking ("open" mode)
claim.awaits: whom it waits for: "office" — the office, "host" — the host of the slot; null — nobody
claim.host: true — this person is the host of the slot (picks the others)
claim.name: who: first and last name or the name of the place from the link (opened in this browser); null — no name
claim.group: one request for several things at once (e.g. a house and a chapel) has the same "group"

format.intro:
Reservations in one document: resources (a priest's time, a hall, a house) with their rules and slots to choose, and in the export also the reservations the office sees.
What the import does (Reservations → “More” → “Import and export (JSON)”):
- First it shows the list of changes and the warnings; it saves only after “Import”.
- A resource or slot with an "id" from the export is changed in place — only the keys present in the document; what is absent stays. Empty text ("") clears a field. Without "id" a new one is created. An "id" that does not exist (or a slot already past) is skipped with a warning.
- It deletes nothing. It does not change reservations ("claims") — they are in the export for reading only.
- You can change and create only in areas you write in; the export only shows the rest.
- The title, place, note and link of a slot are sealed in this browser with the area's key — as when saving in the calendar.
- Whether someone may take a slot is decided by the service at each reservation, by the resource's rules — the import only saves rules and slots.
- Changing the time of a slot that already has reservations: the reservations move with it (the n-th day of the series to the n-th day of the new one), and those left without a day are declined; days cancelled or moved one by one return to the rhythm of the series. The preview warns about every such slot, about a number of places smaller than those taken, about a slot that stops being choosable, and about a new slot during an existing reservation.
- The export covers slots from yesterday {days} days ahead (also series running in that time) and reservations from that time.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

Document:
{top}
format.slotText:
A slot to choose is a meeting in the calendar of an "offered" resource — single or a series, as in the Calendar. The time is local (as in this browser's calendar).
{keys}
format.claimText:
A reservation — only in the export and only for reading: the import skips it. They are answered in Reservations or in the Calendar (“To confirm”).
{keys}
format.usage:
- An "offered" resource: its slots are meetings in the resource's calendar. On a page the module “Reservation” (field “What can be reserved”) shows them with the button “Choose this slot”. An "open" resource: the same module shows what is taken and asks for one's own time.
- A slot can be taken by a person with their own link or signed in (for whom — chosen at the top of the page). Anyone who sees the module sees what is free and what is taken — never who took it. "reserveArea" closes the slots to people outside that group (and the groups under it).
- Requests waiting for the office ("approval": "office") are seen by those who write in the resource's area: in Reservations (“Waiting for an answer”), in the Calendar (“To confirm”), in the bell and in “Waiting for you” (“Reservations to confirm”). Requests to join ("inviteHours") are seen by the host in the module “Reservation”.
- In the Calendar the slots to choose are ordinary appointments with the number of places taken (“2/3”); without a title they carry the resource's name. A signed-in person has their reservation in their own Calendar (“This is your reservation”).
- A form step completed “by itself — when the person chooses a slot” is done when the person has a request or reservation for this resource.
- There are no push notifications about reservations: the person sees the answer — also a cancelled slot — at their slot in the module “Reservation”.

myTerm.noHost: No — everyone can sign up for the free places right away.
myTerm.deadline: If you do not answer by {until}, the slot opens for everyone.
myTerm.hosting: You are the host of this slot until {until}.

hostLeft.other: Until then the {count} free places can only be taken by people with your code or those you accept. After that — if there are fewer of you than {min} — they open for everyone.

myTerm.codeGone: The code was only visible when signing up — it can no longer be read.

myTerm.unhostConfirm: The free places will be open to everyone at once, and your code will stop working.
myTerm.unhostAsks: People who asked to join will be accepted in turn as long as there are places.
myTerm.unhostYes: Yes, I give up the host rights
myTerm.resignLead: Don't want to invite anyone? Give up the host rights — the free places open for everyone at once.
myTerm.hostOverKept: The host time ended {at} — your group is complete, the slot stays yours.
myTerm.hostOverOpen: The host time ended {at} — the free places are open to everyone.
myTerm.leaveConfirm: Really give up this slot? The place will be freed for others.
myTerm.closedByOffice: The office closed this slot — nobody else can sign up.
myTerm.closedByYou: You closed this slot — nobody else can sign up and it will not open for others.
